# Verifying Text-to-SQL Queries under Changing Business Semantics

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#changing-business-semantics)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.41090v1) · arXiv v1, 30 October 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 22 PDF pages: Sections 1-10, all controlled/pilot/confirmatory tables and recorded deviations, Appendices A-E, supported policy/schema, reproduction and qualification boundaries.

## Research question

SQL retained after a business-definition change can execute and match the current snapshot while implementing the wrong requested revision on other admissible data.

## Method

An explicit profile binds policy revision, report interval and knowledge cutoff to exact monetary semantics and legal synthetic ledgers. Obligation coverage selects counterexamples under a fixed budget; a separate implementation freezes finite-suite labels and replays decisions.

## Evaluation

Authored mutations establish mechanism behavior; a 24-family pilot uses two local model/runtime bundles and repeated samples. A locally preregistered confirmation uses 32 new authored families, 192 query-definition cells, eight-ledger arms and family-level paired inference. Native tools are qualified separately rather than ranked as full competing systems.

## What the results support

The confirmation detects 137/144 nonconforming cells versus 127/144 with generic ordering; 63 errors agree on the initial snapshot. Current-obligation and equal-weight ablations also detect 137, identifying coverage rather than revision-specific weighting as the measured benefit.

## Limits and qualifications

Approval of policy semantics remains external. The schema, revisions and ledgers are authored; two local bundles do not establish enterprise transfer. Zero rejections of finite-suite-agreeing cases follow the replay/suite relationship and do not prove population false-rejection control. Preregistration timestamps are local, with a disclosed 74-versus-81 candidate-pool deviation; raw artifacts lack a public identifier.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Clarifies when verification should reject, retain finite evidence or request clarification after semantic change, without treating every historical query as stale.
